summary: Diane Bazella, 64, of Minnetonka, Minnesota, spent Christmas with her birth mother Sherri Geerts, 81, after a nearly 40-year search that revealed she was likely switched at birth in 1960. A 2017 home DNA test showed no match to her known relatives and led, over several years, to the discovery that her birth certificate was wrong. The two women now speak often, visit several times a year, and share many traits, though how the switch happened may never be known.
one_line: After decades of searching and a DNA test, Diane Bazella found she was switched at birth and now spends holidays with birth mother Sherri Geerts.
key_facts: Diane Bazella, 64, of Minnetonka, Minnesota, searched nearly 40 years for her birth family and found her birth mother, Sherri Geerts, 81, of Sunnyvale, California.
Bazella first found Geerts in May 2021, heard her voice by phone on Christmas Day 2021, and met her in person in July 2022.
Bazella was adopted at nine months old in 1961 by Walter and Ila Peterson of Edina, Minnesota, and was told of the adoption at age five.
She was born at Booth Memorial Hospital (now the Booth Brown House Youth Shelter) in St. Paul, Minnesota, a Salvation Army facility for unwed mothers.
At 23, Bazella used public birth records to find a woman she thought was her birth mother, who said her birth name was Kelly Jean; that woman died in 2000 and the two never had a strong bond.
In 2017 Bazella took a home DNA test that matched none of her known relatives, and she spent four years contacting genealogy matches without success.
One close DNA match emailed back, and after more than a year of work her father admitted fathering a baby girl in 1960 with Sherri Nordlie, now Geerts.
Two baby girls, Kelly Jean and Dawn Marie, were born within hours of each other on Sept. 29 at the hospital; Bazella was actually Dawn Marie.
Bazella said, "I lost 39 years … There's a lot of grieving with that," and she may never learn how the switch happened.
Geerts had her baby at age 18 and remembers naming and dressing her before she was taken away; she thought of her daughter every year on her birthday.
The two share habits like keeping lists, constantly applying lipstick, collecting garden gnomes, and having the same sense of humor.
Bazella has met all four of her siblings and has a relationship with her birth father, Victor Rebeck, 84.
Geerts hopes to live "like a hundred years at least" to make up for lost time.
